details.description: Secrets (PAYMENT_TOKEN, MAIL_SERVER_KEY, INTERNAL_AUTH) are hard-coded in source, exposing sensitive credentials and making rotation difficult.
details.fix_explanation: Move all sensitive values to environment variables and/or a secure secrets manager. The secure code reads PAYMENT_TOKEN, MAIL_SERVER_KEY and INTERNAL_AUTH from the environment and fails safely if missing.
details.secure_code_snippet:
PAYMENT_TOKEN = os.environ.get("PAYMENT_TOKEN")
MAIL_SERVER_KEY = os.environ.get("MAIL_SERVER_KEY")
INTERNAL_AUTH = os.environ.get("INTERNAL_AUTH")

details.description: The code constructs SQL with string formatting using user-provided uid, allowing injection and data leakage.
details.fix_explanation: Use parameterized queries so user input is passed as parameters instead of interpolated into SQL. Also validate uid type and use exceptions for errors.
details.secure_code_snippet:
q = "SELECT id,name,balance FROM profiles WHERE id = ?"
c.execute(q, (uid,))

details.description: The application will make HTTP requests to any user-provided notify_url. This can be abused to reach internal services and exfiltrate data.
details.fix_explanation: Validate and restrict notify endpoints. Require HTTPS, a configured host allow-list, limit request timeouts, and handle request exceptions gracefully.

details.description: The function update_records reads any file path supplied by the user, enabling reading of sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd).
details.fix_explanation: Restrict config reads to a controlled configuration directory and verify paths using absolute resolution to prevent traversal or arbitrary reads.

details.description: export_data constructs a shell command using user-controlled 'name' and calls subprocess with shell=True, enabling arbitrary command execution.
details.fix_explanation: Avoid shell calls and use the zipfile module to create zip archives safely; validate the name against an allowlist pattern before using.
details.secure_code_snippet:
if not _safe_filename(name): raise ValueError('invalid name')
with zipfile.ZipFile(out_name, 'w') as zf: zf.write(DB_FILE, arcname=os.path.basename(DB_FILE))

details.description: auth_user uses MD5 hashing which is cryptographically weak and unsuitable for auth tokens. It's also combined with a hard-coded secret.
details.fix_explanation: Use HMAC-SHA256 or a secure token library (or JWT) and read secrets from a protected environment instead of hard-coding.

details.description: Running the Flask app with debug=True exposes the interactive debugger and remote code execution if reachable by attackers.
details.fix_explanation: Control debug via environment variable and ensure debug mode is disabled in production deployments (default False).

details.description: The code prints transfer logs containing targets and amounts which could leak sensitive info to logs.
details.fix_explanation: Use structured logging with appropriate log levels and avoid printing secrets. Scrub or classify logs so sensitive fields are not stored.
details.secure_code_snippet: logger.info('transfer request for target=%s amount=%s', target, amount_f)  # don't log tokens
